bull_bear.body: Prioritizing advertising & digital spends (up 34% YoY); reinvesting in brand portfolio (non-ADHO); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; acquisitions not required for INR500cr goal but could be top-up
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Input cost volatility (LLP, packaging, copra, mustard); potential need for frontal pricing; international market recovery timeline; execution risk in scaling non-ADHO brands; channel inventory normalization risk (denied by management)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, execution-focused, disciplined on margins; no guidance given on future metrics; acknowledges inflation risks but asserts control via pricing, mix, inventory; strong belief in ADHO and portfolio diversification
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Project Aarohan delivers 2-3% growth delta in covered states; Banjara’s profitability improvement tied to scale, not cost integration; 98% of value-added hair oil is ADHO; no channel filling despite GST stability; inventory levels lean at distributor level
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Balance sheet remains near debt-free (consolidated finance cost only INR 1.6 Cr for FY26) and investment-heavy, with substantial current and non-current financial investments held against ~INR 755 Cr total equity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: ADHO: 20s% full-year revenue growth, mid-single digit volume growth (unadjusted), double-digit MLH-adjusted volume growth; Non-ADHO portfolio: INR225cr revenue in FY26, targeting INR500cr in 3 years; Banjara’s: double-digit growth, low-teen margin; Coconut: key growth pillar within non-ADHO; International: Nepal profitable, Bangladesh breakeven; GT: high-teens growth (urban 20s%, rural mid-teens%); OT: 30% of total sales, growing 20s% YoY; CSD/CPC: muted
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Anchors the story on the flagship ADHO (Almond Drops Hair Oil) franchise, which grew in the twenties for full-year FY26 and delivered near double-digit volume growth in the quarter after accounting for ml-age reductions.
- Frames a diversification narrative via a 'Growth Portfolio' (Coconut largest, then Banjara's) that now contributes ~INR 225 Cr annual sales and is net-contribution positive.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [International] Focus markets Nepal and Bangladesh grew at both quarter and year level, with Nepal profitability improving and Bangladesh reaching breakeven; RoW and GCC & Africa stayed weak, and new IB leadership is expected to drive sequential improvement over the next 2 quarters.
- [Balance sheet] Consolidated Other Intangible Assets rose sharply from INR 0.6 Cr to INR 103.2 Cr in FY26, indicating a brand/intangible acquisition the deck does not explain.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: revenue: +28% YoY (standalone), +32% YoY (consolidated); EBITDA/margin: +131% YoY to INR78cr, 25% margin (standalone); PAT (rptd): +135% YoY to INR63.6cr (consolidated); PAT (normalized): no material one-offs; order book: not applicable; net debt: net cash position implied by strong cash flow, no debt mentioned
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin: 63% in Q4, 60% FY26 (+650 bps YoY); driven by pricing, mix, MLH adjustments; input cost pressure from LLP, packaging, mustard, copra; no cost inflation hit in Q4 due to inventory buffer; margin sustainability targeted in low-to-mid 20s EBITDA range despite inflation
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: no formal guidance; margin: targets low-to-mid 20s EBITDA margin range; order inflow: not applicable; capex/commissioning: no capex guidance, focus on distribution and brand investment
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Scaling non-ADHO portfolio (Banjara’s, Coconut) to INR500cr in 3 years; expanding Project Aarohan to 5 new states; new brand launches; international recovery in MENA/Rest of World
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Bajaj Consumer delivered a breakthrough Q4 with 28% standalone revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion to 25% driven by ADHO volume gains, mix improvement, and MLH adjustments, setting a new base for sustained profitability; the company is now focused on scaling its non-ADHO portfolio to INR500cr in 3 years while navigating input cost volatility without compromising margin discipline.

open.item: New GST-benefit-priced stock is expected to fully reach the retail trade by November-December 2025, following primary-level transition between September-October.
Nepal business had a temporary setback from political instability in Aug-Sep 2025; management expects it to normalize very soon and get back on track.
Integration of the Banjara (Vishal Personal Care) portfolio with Bajaj Personal Care into the remaining southern states will be completed over the next quarter.

Management expects Project Aarohan's rural rollout (currently disruptive/underperforming) to also turn into a 'green' (successful) status in a couple more quarters, versus urban/wholesale which are already strong.

War in the Gulf has caused extreme volatility in LLP and packaging material prices and delayed cooling in mustard and copra; management will freeze its cost/pricing strategy as the situation unfolds over the next month or so.
Management will take some amount of frontal pricing action in the current quarter (Q1FY27) to manage margins amid cost inflation, in addition to MLH adjustments already taken.
Due to input cost inflation, the company will take some frontal pricing in Q1FY27 and has already taken MLH adjustments in Q4.
Management flagged ongoing structural go-to-market issues in international markets (GCC/Africa/KSA distributor transition) but expects resolution within the next couple of quarters.
Management will provide clarity on strategic direction (focus vs. phase-out) for the non-core smaller portfolio brands (7-8 products) over the next 2-3 quarters.
Project Aarohan's third phase, covering five new states not previously covered, began at the end of Q4FY26 and will be executed through FY27.
Execute the third phase of Project Aarohan in five new states during FY27 to drive distribution and growth.

Management is prioritizing portfolio streamlining and reviving ADHO growth first, with more innovative new product launches expected mainly in the next fiscal year rather than in the remainder of FY26.
ADHO (core brand) is being planned to grow at least at a mid-single-digit CAGR over the next two-three years.
For products sold across GT, MT and e-commerce, management targets at least INR50 crores in revenue over a three-year period from launch.
Management expects the Almond Drops Hair & Skin Care extension portfolio to become a substantial contributor to revenue and profit within the next 2-3 years.

Existing plants have capacity headroom for 2-3 years of growth and no significant capex commitment is planned over the next couple of years, though management reserves the right to revisit for manufacturing efficiency.
Management intends to grow the non-ADHO 'growth portfolio' to around INR500 crores in size over the next three years.
Non-ADHO growth portfolio needs to achieve a ~30% CAGR to reach INR500 crores in 3 years from a base of INR225 crores in FY26.
Grow the non-ADHO (growth) portfolio to around INR500 crores in size over the next three years.
Non-ADHO portfolio (currently ~18% of revenue) is targeted to reach 40% of total revenue within the next 4-5 years.

revisions.item: Quick commerce currently contributes only about 6% salience to overall sales; management expects this to scale up much more strongly going forward.
Management aspires to further improve overall margins on a medium-to-long-term basis and will manage new-product mix to protect that margin trajectory.
Company aspires to operate EBITDA margin in the low-20s to mid-20s percent range on an ongoing basis.
